kettle: A person stands at a kitchen counter, pours hot water from a kettle into a mug, puts the kettle down, then holds the mug with both hands to warm them and takes a sip.
chop: A person stands at a kitchen counter and chops vegetables on a cutting board with a knife in the right hand, holding the vegetable with the left hand, at a steady natural pace.
stoke: A person crouches in front of a small wood stove, opens its little door with the right hand, puts a log inside with both hands, closes the door and stands up.
sharpen: A person stands at a workbench and sharpens a knife on a whetstone, sliding the blade back and forth with the right hand while the left hand holds the stone.
lantern: A person stands at a workbench holding an old lantern with the left hand and repairs it with small precise movements of the right hand, turning it to look at it.
diary: A person sits at a table and writes in a notebook with a pen in the right hand, pauses to think with the pen near the chin, then keeps writing.
sweep: A person sweeps the floor with a broom held in both hands, short sweeping strokes, taking small steps forward.
water: A person holds a watering can in the right hand and waters a potted plant on a shelf at waist height, then lowers the can.
listen: A person stands at a window, leans slightly forward and listens warily, freezes, slowly turns the head, then relaxes a little.
bolt: A person stands at a door, pulls the door handle with the right hand to test it, then slides a bolt firmly closed and nods.
count: A person stands in front of a shelf and counts the supplies on it, pointing at the items one by one with the right index finger.
radio: A person stands at a table, leans slightly towards a small old radio and slowly turns its knob with the right hand, listening with the head tilted.
telescope: A person stands and looks through a telescope on a tripod, holding it with both hands, and slowly pans it from left to right and back.
dangle: A person sits on the edge of a high platform with the legs dangling over the edge, hands resting beside the hips, swinging the legs slowly and looking around.
carrylogs: A person walks forward at a normal pace carrying an armful of firewood logs held with both arms against the chest.
carrysack: A person walks forward at a normal pace carrying a heavy sack over the right shoulder, holding it with the right hand.
droplogs: A person holding an armful of logs bends the knees and puts the logs down onto a pile on the floor, then stands up straight.
picklog: A person bends down, picks up one log from a pile on the floor with both hands and stands up holding it in front of the body.
fridgein: A person opens a refrigerator door with the right hand, puts a package inside with the left hand onto a shelf, and closes the door.
fridgeout: A person opens a refrigerator door with the right hand, takes a package out with the left hand and closes the door with the right hand.
eat: A person sits at a table and eats from a plate with a spoon in the right hand, bringing food to the mouth and chewing.
jacketon: A person takes a jacket off a wall hook with the right hand, puts the left arm into the sleeve, swings the jacket behind the back, puts the right arm into the other sleeve and straightens the collar.
jacketoff: A person takes off a jacket, pulling the arms out of the sleeves one at a time, and hangs it on a wall hook in front of them.
bowtake: A person reaches up to a wall hook, takes down a bow with the left hand, slings a quiver over the right shoulder with the right hand and adjusts the strap.
bowhang: A person takes a quiver off the shoulder and hangs it on a wall hook, then hangs a bow on the hook next to it.
scratch: A person stands and scratches the back of the head with the right hand, thinking, then lowers the hand.
